```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE, error = FALSE)
r <- params$report
p <- r$priorities
esc <- function(x) as.character(htmltools::htmlEscape(x))
```

The Steamboat Island feasibility report anticipates an additional mussel-habitat benefit from stone protection. This pilot examines the scientific basis for that expectation and the evidence needed to evaluate it locally. **The current record supports an anticipated benefit, not a demonstrated post-construction mussel outcome.**

## The Steamboat Island pilot

```{r question, results='asis'}
cat('<div class="question"><strong>Pilot question — ', esc(r$question_basis), '</strong><p>', esc(r$question), '</p></div>')
report_table(data.frame(Item=c('Restoration intent','Project stage in the supplied record','Monitoring commitment'),
  Understanding=c(r$mussel_benefit$classification,
    'Construction ongoing; baseline/construction monitoring reported by the user. This report does not update construction status.',
    paste('Dedicated post-construction mussel surveys:',r$mussel_benefit$dedicated_postconstruction_mussel_surveys))))
```

Mussel habitat is an **ancillary benefit**, separate from the project's formal objectives and performance criteria. The absence of post-construction performance data at this stage is not evidence of failure. The absence of a dedicated mussel-survey commitment is a separate planning consideration.

## Restoration intent and the expected response

The recommended plan describes potential additional fish/mussel habitat associated with stone protection (feasibility report VI-1, PDF p. 133). Table X-3 footnote 8 (X-4, PDF p. 169) does not commit dedicated post-construction mussel surveys. The final feature design, installation identity and local mussel response have not been reconciled in this pilot.

```{r pilot-path, fig.width=10, fig.height=2.8, fig.alt='Proposed pathway from a restoration feature to local hydraulic and substrate conditions and then an expected mussel response. Both arrows represent unverified local links.'}
report_pilot_path(r)
```

**How to read the diagram:** the arrows identify relationships to investigate. They do not establish that a feature has produced the expected conditions or that mussels have responded. Persistence, survival, recruitment and habitat occupancy are related but distinct possible responses; the pilot has not selected a local endpoint or numerical success threshold.

## What the science contributes

The following extracts help explain why substrate and hydraulic conditions warrant investigation. Most are based on abstracts; they retain the source studies' inference limits and have not received SME review.

```{r focused-science, results='asis'}
ids <- c('SC-02','SC-03','SC-05')
a <- r$assertions[match(ids,r$assertions$id),]
report_table(data.frame(Reference=paste(a$id,a$source_id,sep=' / '),
  `Scientific contribution`=a$paraphrase,`Limit on use at Steamboat Island`=a$limit,check.names=FALSE))
```

The hydraulic interpretation and habitat-dependent survival findings informed the following **proposed local hypothesis**, SC-08. It is an assistant formulation for review, not a verbatim author statement or a hypothesis known to have been adopted by the project's designers.

```{r local-hypothesis, results='asis'}
h <- r$assertions[r$assertions$id=='SC-08',]
cat('<div class="question"><strong>SC-08 — proposed local hypothesis</strong><p>',esc(h$paraphrase),'</p></div>')
```

```{r derivations, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5, fig.alt='SC-02 and SC-03 inform the formulation of SC-08; this relationship is not proof of a local restoration effect.'}
report_derivations(r)
```

These links explain the hypothesis's origin. Applying the research to Steamboat Island still requires review of the study locations, species, flow regimes, methods and relevance to the local intervention. No sampled publication is asserted here to have evaluated Steamboat Island.

```{r scientific-instance, results='asis'}
si <- r$study_instance
if (!is.null(si)) {
  cat('<h3>Tracing one study: what survival and growth tell us</h3>',
    '<p>MS-03 (Newton et al. 2020) can now be traced into its public data release. ',
    'The inspected sources distinguish the comparison, repeated observations, reported findings and local interpretation. ',
    'Full-text model details remain unverified.</p>')
  report_table(si$chain[c(2,3,4,7,8),c('object','record','locator')])
  cat('<p><strong>Implication for this pilot:</strong> survival and growth are distinct responses. ',
    'A habitat contrast in one does not establish the same contrast in the other. ',
    'This study informs a local question; it does not establish a Steamboat restoration effect.</p>',
    '<p><strong>Source reconciliation needed:</strong> the narrative reports 578 tagged mussels; ',
    'the tracking file contains 569 individual IDs, and the 2012 plot placement counts sum to 576. ',
    'These totals have been preserved separately. Their differences are unresolved, and no new vital rates were calculated.</p>')
}
```

## What would let us evaluate the benefit here

| Part of the evidence chain | Current pilot record | Next useful work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restoration feature and location | Ancillary intent is documented; actual feature identity/design/installation is unresolved | Review final design and available as-built/GIS records; identify the feature and habitat area to evaluate |
| Habitat conditions and mechanism | Hydraulic/substrate reasoning comes from research; local change has not been demonstrated | Review local flow and substrate evidence across relevant conditions and compare it with the studies' scope |
| Mussel population and response | Baseline/construction monitoring is reported, but mussel-specific observations and analyses are not assembled in this pilot | Identify species, existing surveys, sampling periods and measured responses; assess suitability for the question |
| Study design and inference | No local comparison design or demonstrated post-construction effect is established | Determine an appropriate comparison, timing, analysis and treatment of alternative explanations before drawing conclusions |

The feasibility report identifies the annual interagency Cordova Mussel Blitz as a possible external data opportunity. Availability and suitability need checking; it is not a guaranteed dataset or a dedicated project task.

## Next steps for this pilot

1. **Confirm the local restoration connection.** Identify the relevant feature, location, design intent and available construction evidence.
2. **Resolve the scientific transfer questions.** The MS-03 source-to-data instance is now available below. Reconcile its cohort counts, verify full-paper analysis and substrate metrics, and review applicability alongside MS-02.
3. **Assess the evidence that could answer the question.** Inventory local mussel/habitat data and identify the smallest useful analysis or study-design increment, including any missing observations and review responsibilities.

The next deliverable should be one inspectable chain from restoration expectation through scientific reasoning to available observations and remaining needs. It should help partners decide whether existing data can address the expectation or whether additional work is justified. This report creates no new monitoring commitment.

<summary>Conceptual entities and formal project objectives</summary>

The entities are candidate distinctions for data-model development. They are not approved tables or ontology classes. Formal project objectives remain separate from the ancillary mussel benefit.

```{r entities-and-objectives, results='asis'}
report_table(r$entities)
report_table(r$objectives)
report_table(data.frame(Item=names(r$project_connection),Record=vapply(r$project_connection,
  function(x) if(is.null(x)) NA_character_ else paste(unlist(x),collapse='; '),'')))
```

The existing conceptual chain is HREP → Project Objective → Performance Criterion → Monitoring Task → Observation. Production observation storage and cross-system identities remain unverified. Existing USACE document, provenance, temporal, spatial and SOSA patterns provide the organizational baseline.

```{r full-priority-register, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(p)) {
  agenda <- p$questions[c('local_id','question','restoration_goal','restoration_objective')]
  names(agenda) <- c('Question','Original wording','Workshop restoration goal','Workshop restoration objective')
  report_table(agenda)
  ranks <- p$questions[c('local_id',p$rank_fields)]
  names(ranks) <- c('Question',p$reach_labels)
  report_table(ranks)
  if(nrow(p$marks)) report_table(p$marks)
}
```

Ranks remain reach-specific; no system-wide score is calculated. Reported n values are not interpreted as confirmed participant counts. An x records an association of unresolved meaning, not a completed test. Source groupings are not automatically strategic-plan or individual HREP objectives. WQ identifiers are review-local and tied to the source edition.

</details>
